teaches: Why something matters: open on what it is in one concrete line; the reason in numbers; then the moment it failed and the history that made it contested; the forecast is left out; land where it matters now.

packet.title: The Suez Canal and world trade
sentences: The Suez Canal is about a hundred and twenty miles long and crosses Egypt between the Red Sea and the Mediterranean.
It spares ships between Asia and Europe the voyage around Africa, which adds thousands of miles and more than a week.
Roughly twelve percent of world trade passes through it.
Canal fees are one of Egypt's biggest sources of foreign currency.
Analysts expect traffic through the canal to grow over the next decade.

packet.title: Ever Given blocks the canal
sentences: The container ship Ever Given ran aground across the canal in a sandstorm and blocked it for six days.
Hundreds of ships queued and some turned to sail around Africa.

packet.title: The Suez crisis
sentences: Egypt's president Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalised the canal in 1956.
Britain, France and Israel invaded and withdrew under pressure from the United States and the Soviet Union.
